mainTopic: גרירה (one offering 'drawing along' atonement for linked sins): how a חטאת for reaping and grinding on שבת covers acts done in different kinds of שגגה, and whether two half-measures done in different kinds of שגגה combine.
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing רבא's ruling about a person who reaped and ground twice on שבת. The first time he forgot it was שבת (שגגת שבת), and the second time he did not know the acts were forbidden (שגגת מלאכות). One offering can 'draw along' (גרירה) atonement for linked acts. But if he learns of the acts in the reverse order, רבא says the second grinding is not covered. אביי says that grinding is covered too. The גמרא asks how רבא can use גרירה when he rejected it in a case about eating חלב. It answers that רבא accepted גרירה from אביי, but not a 'draw of a draw' (גרירה דגרירה). Next, רבי זירא rules that half-measures done in the two kinds of שגגה do not combine, because they need separate חטאות. The גמרא challenges this rule from a משנה about half-olives eaten from two dishes, following רבי יהושע. It answers that ריש לקיש's explanation belongs on the סיפא of that משנה, so the rule stands. The עמוד ends as the גמרא begins a new inference from that reading, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Reaping draws reaping, grinding draws grinding
steps.stepSummary: Continuing רבא's ruling: when he becomes aware of the acts done in שגגת שבת first, the offering covers them and also draws along the matching acts done in שגגת מלאכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reaping draws reaping, and grinding draws grinding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבא's ruling. He first learned about the reaping and grinding he did while forgetting it was שבת. His offering for those acts also covers the second reaping and the second grinding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reaping and grinding count as one sin, because both fall under one 'forgetting שבת'. The offering for the first reaping also covers the second reaping, since both are the same מלאכה. In the same way, the first grinding covers the second grinding. So one offering covers all four acts.

keyTerms.meaning: Reaping, a forbidden מלאכה on שבת
Grinding, a forbidden מלאכה on שבת
Draws along, meaning its atonement also covers another linked act
Doing a forbidden act while forgetting that today is שבת

steps.confusionAlert: 'Drawing' does not mean one act causes the other. It means the single קרבן brought for one act also brings atonement for a linked act.

phrases.english: Reaping draws along reaping,
phrases.notes: The offering for the first reaping covers the second reaping (same מלאכה).

phrases.english: and grinding draws along grinding.
phrases.notes: The first grinding covers the second grinding.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's statement begun on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When he becomes aware first of the שגגת שבת acts, a single offering covers all four acts by way of גרירה.

steps.title: Reverse order: the second grinding is left out
steps.stepSummary: If he first becomes aware of the reaping done in זדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות, the offering covers the earlier reaping and the grinding done with it. The second grinding stays uncovered.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he first became aware of the reaping done while knowing it was שבת but not knowing the acts were forbidden, the reaping draws along the earlier reaping and the grinding done together with it. The matching grinding stays in its place, uncovered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now describes what happens when the person learns about the acts in the opposite order. This time, one grinding is not covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second reaping draws along the first reaping, since both are the same מלאכה. The first reaping is linked to the first grinding, because both were done while forgetting שבת. But the second grinding is not directly linked to anything that was atoned for, so it needs its own קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Knowing that it is שבת
Not knowing that these particular acts are forbidden
The parallel one, here the second grinding
Stays in its place, meaning it is not atoned for

phrases.english: But if he became aware of the reaping
done intentionally regarding שבת but unwittingly regarding the labors,
the reaping draws along the earlier reaping and the grinding done with it,
phrases.notes: The earlier reaping and grinding were tied together because they both happened during one stretch of forgetting it was שבת.

phrases.english: and the parallel grinding remains in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל נוֹדַע לוֹ עַל קְצִירָה שֶׁל זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the reverse order of awareness with the order in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the reverse order, the second grinding is not atoned for.

steps.title: אביי: the second grinding is covered too
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees with רבא and says the grinding that was drawn along also draws along the other grinding.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Grinding also draws grinding, because the name 'grinding' is one.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי argues with the last part of רבא's ruling. He says even the second grinding is covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both grindings carry the same name and count as the same מלאכה. So once the first grinding is atoned for, it pulls the second grinding along with it. This happens even though the first grinding itself was only covered by being drawn along.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
One name, meaning one category of מלאכה

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Grinding also draws along grinding,
since the designation of grinding is one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: טְחִינָה נָמֵי גּוֹרֶרֶת טְחִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the end of רבא's ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אביי, a grinding that was atoned for through drawing can itself draw along another grinding.

steps.title: Does רבא even accept drawing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא by pointing to a known dispute about eating חלב, where רבא seems to reject גרירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבא really hold of 'drawing'? But it was stated: Someone ate two olive-sized pieces of חלב in one lapse of awareness. He became aware of one of them. Then he ate another olive-size while still unaware about the second piece.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבא can use גרירה here. It sets up a case about forbidden fat where רבא's view seems to go the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case, piece 1 and piece 2 were eaten in one lapse of awareness, and piece 2 and piece 3 were eaten in another. But piece 1 and piece 3 share nothing directly. The case tests whether an offering can reach a sin that is only connected through a 'middle' sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Drawing, meaning atonement carried along to a linked sin
Forbidden animal fat
The size of an olive, the minimum amount for a punishment or offering
A lapse of awareness, a period of not knowing

phrases.english: And does Rava hold of drawing?
But wasn't it stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל שְׁנֵי זֵיתֵי חֵלֶב בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: He ate two olive-bulks of forbidden fat in one lapse of awareness,
and he became aware of one of them,
and then he again ate an olive-bulk
during the lapse of awareness of the second.
phrases.notes: Pieces 2 and 3 both happened during the same stretch of forgetting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרָבָא גְּרִירָה? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's use of גרירה in steps 1 and 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of גרירה in the שבת case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the חלב case, רבא rules that atonement does not pass from piece 1 to piece 3. That suggests he rejects גרירה.

steps.title: רבא's ruling in the חלב case
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that an offering only covers pieces that share a lapse of awareness with the piece it was brought for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he brought an offering for the first piece, the first and second are atoned for, but the third is not. If he brought it for the third, the third and second are atoned for, but the first is not. If he brought it for the middle one, all of them are atoned for.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the evidence for the challenge. רבא lets an offering cover only the pieces that are directly linked to the piece it was brought for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Piece 1 does not reach piece 3, so רבא does not allow drawing through a middle link. The middle piece covers everything only because it is directly linked to both of the others. That is not גרירה.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering, here a חטאת
Are atoned for
The middle one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the 'middle piece covers all' ruling proves רבא accepts גרירה. The middle piece is directly linked to both of the others.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he brought an offering for the first,
the first and second are atoned for,
the third is not atoned for.
If he brought an offering for the third,
the third and second are atoned for,
the first is not atoned for.
If he brought an offering for the middle one,
all of them are atoned for.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן עַל רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies רבא's ruling that drives the challenge.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's ruling in the case of the three pieces of חלב

steps.title: אביי: any one offering covers all
steps.stepSummary: In the same cited dispute, אביי holds that an offering for any piece covers all three pieces by גרירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Even if he brought an offering for any one of them, all of them are atoned for.
steps.whatsHappening: This completes the quoted dispute. It shows that אביי is the one who holds of גרירה, which makes רבא look like he does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, piece 1 draws piece 2, and piece 2 draws piece 3. Placed next to רבא's view, this sharpens the question: how could רבא use גרירה in the שבת case?

keyTerms.meaning: Even
All of them

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן עַל אֶחָד מֵהֶן —
phrases.english: Even if he brought an offering for one of them,
all of them are atoned for.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ הֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן עַל אֶחָד מֵהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the cited dispute, contrasting אביי with רבא.
steps.raayaObject: That גרירה is אביי's view, not רבא's
steps.raayaSupportSource: אביי's opinion in the חלב dispute

steps.title: רבא adopted אביי's view
steps.stepSummary: The answer: after hearing גרירה from אביי, רבא accepted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he heard it from אביי, he agreed with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. רבא changed his mind after hearing אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חלב ruling was רבא's earlier view. His שבת ruling came later, after he accepted גרירה from אביי. So the two rulings do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: After he heard it
He agreed with it, he adopted it

phrases.english: After he heard it from Abaye, he adopted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 4 to 6.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא later accepted גרירה from אביי.

steps.title: Then grinding should draw grinding too
steps.stepSummary: If רבא accepts גרירה, he should agree with אביי that the second grinding is covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, grinding should also draw along grinding!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. If רבא now accepts drawing, why does he leave the second grinding uncovered in step 2?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבא accepts אביי's principle, it seems he should also accept אביי's conclusion in step 3. This challenge targets the end of רבא's ruling, where the second grinding 'stays in its place'.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
It should draw along

phrases.english: If so,
grinding should also draw along grinding!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, טְחִינָה נָמֵי תִּגְרֹר לִטְחִינָה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the parallel grinding stays uncovered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבא accepts גרירה, he should agree with אביי's ruling in step 3.

steps.title: Drawing yes, a draw of a draw no
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts one level of גרירה but not a second level built on top of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds of drawing, but he does not hold of a 'drawing of drawing'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly where רבא stops. A sin that was only covered by being drawn along cannot itself draw along another sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first grinding was covered only because it was drawn along through the first reaping. For it to then draw along the second grinding would be a second step of drawing, which רבא rejects. אביי allows this chain.

keyTerms.meaning: A drawing of a drawing, a second level of carried-over atonement
He does not hold of it

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: one step of גרירה, but no גרירה דגרירה. אביי: גרירה even in a chain.

phrases.english: He holds of drawing,
he does not hold of a drawing of drawing.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּרִירָה אִית לֵיהּ, גְּרִירָה דִגְרִירָה לֵית לֵיהּ
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accepting גרירה means accepting it at every level.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא accepts only direct גרירה, not a second level.

steps.title: What was obvious to אביי and רבא was a question for רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: A transition line: the גמרא notes that רבי זירא was unsure about something אביי and רבא took for granted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Something that was obvious to אביי and רבא was a question for רבי זירא.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to bring רבי זירא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי and רבא assumed that שגגת שבת and שגגת מלאכות are not separate for חטאות, so one offering can cover both, as in רבא's ruling above. רבי זירא was not sure about this. His question about combining half-measures will test that point.

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious
Was a question, an unresolved doubt

phrases.english: A matter that was obvious to Abaye and Rava
was a dilemma for Rabbi Zeira.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא דִּפְשִׁיטָא לְהוּ לְאַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא מִבַּעְיָא לְרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Transitions from the אביי and רבא discussion to רבי זירא's question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי and רבא took for granted that the two kinds of שגגה are not separate for חטאות.

steps.title: Do two half-measures from different kinds of שגגה combine?
steps.stepSummary: The question: half a גרוגרת was reaped and ground in שגגת שבת, and another half in שגגת מלאכות. Do they add up to one full measure?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked רבי אסי, and some say רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: Someone reaped and ground half a dried-fig's worth while forgetting it was שבת. Then he again reaped and ground half a dried-fig's worth while knowing it was שבת but not knowing the acts were forbidden. Do the two halves combine?
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the actual question. Each half alone is too small to require an offering, so the issue is whether they join into a full amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the two kinds of שגגה form one category, the halves would combine into a full גרוגרת and an offering would be needed. If they are separate categories, the halves would not combine.

keyTerms.meaning: A dried fig, the minimum amount for liability on carrying out food on שבת and for these acts
What is the law?
That they combine

phrases.english: For Rabbi Zeira asked Rabbi Asi,
and some say

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
He reaped and ground half a dried-fig bulk
unwitting about Shabbat but intentional about the labors,
and then again reaped and ground half a dried-fig bulk
intentional about Shabbat but unwitting about the labors,
what is the law: do they combine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the doubt introduced in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether half-measures done in the two different kinds of שגגה combine into one full measure.

steps.title: Separate offerings, so they do not combine
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the two kinds of שגגה require separate חטאות, so their half-measures do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They are separate for sin-offerings, and so they do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered. The two halves stay separate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Full measures done in these two kinds of שגגה would require two separate חטאות. So they are different sins, and half-measures from different sins cannot join. This matches what אביי and רבא assumed.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate
Sin-offerings
Combine

steps.whatToRemember: שגגת שבת and שגגת מלאכות are separate sins, each needing its own חטאת, so half-measures from each do not combine.

phrases.english: He said to him:
They are separate with regard to sin-offerings,
and they do not combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲלוּקִין לַחֲטָאוֹת, וְלֹא מִצְטָרְפִין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are separate for חטאות, so the half-measures do not combine.

steps.title: Challenge: does being separate for חטאות always stop half-measures from combining?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the rule from Step 12 and quotes a משנה about eating חלב, דם, נותר and פגול, which includes a line about two half-olives combining.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that whenever things require separate חטאות, they don't combine? We learned in a משנה: If someone ate חלב and more חלב in one lapse of awareness, he brings only one חטאת. If he ate חלב, דם, נותר and פגול in one lapse, he brings one for each. That is how many types are stricter than one type. And this is how one type is stricter than many types: if he ate half a זית and then another half a זית of one type, he is liable. If the halves were from two types, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule it just stated (separate חטאות means no combining) and brings a משנה as the starting point. The actual contradiction is spelled out a few lines later, in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts one type of forbidden food with many types. Many types give more חטאות, but one type lets half-measures add up. The key line for the challenge is the last one: half-measures of one type combine.

keyTerms.meaning: Separate for sin-offerings: each act would need its own חטאת
They combine (add up to one full measure)
One lapse of awareness (one period of forgetting)
Leftover קרבן meat past its time, and קרבן meat ruined by improper intent
An olive-sized amount, the minimum for liability when eating

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה by itself does not yet contradict anything. The problem only appears after ריש לקיש's explanation (Steps 14-16) shows that this משנה is talking about a case of separate חטאות.

phrases.english: And wherever they are separate for sin-offerings
do they not combine?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
If one ate forbidden fat and more forbidden fat in one lapse of awareness
he is liable for only one.
If he ate forbidden fat, blood, notar and piggul
in one lapse of awareness
he is liable for each and every one.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה חוֹמֶר בְּמִינִין הַרְבֵּה מִמִּין אֶחָד.
phrases.english: This is a stringency of many types over one type.

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה חוֹמֶר בְּמִין אֶחָד מִמִּינִין הַרְבֵּה:
phrases.english: And this is a stringency of one type over many types:
that if he ate half an olive-bulk

phrases.aramaic: וְחָזַר וְאָכַל חֲצִי זַיִת מִמִּין אֶחָד —
phrases.english: and then ate another half olive-bulk of one type
he is liable;
if from two types, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל הֵיכָא דַּחֲלוּקִין לַחֲטָאוֹת לָא מִצְטָרְפִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in Step 12, which said separate חטאות means no combining.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that half-measures do not combine when the acts are חלוקין לחטאות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about eating forbidden foods will be shown to have a case of separate חטאות where halves still combine.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need to say that one type combines?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion: it is obvious that two halves of one type combine, so why does the משנה say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: 'From one type he is liable.' Did that need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls an earlier discussion that asked why the משנה states something so obvious. This sets up ריש לקיש's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two halves of the very same forbidden food clearly add up to a כזית. If the משנה says it anyway, it must be teaching a less obvious case. That pushes us to find a special situation.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (recalling an earlier discussion)
Did it need to be said? (it seems obvious)

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
"From one type he is liable":
was it necessary to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an earlier discussion of the משנה quoted in Step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new idea is taught by saying that halves of one type combine?

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the case is two dishes, following רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the case is one type eaten from two separate dishes. רבי יהושע holds that dishes separate, but only to make things stricter, not more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of בר תוטני: What case are we dealing with? He ate it from two dishes, and the משנה follows רבי יהושע, who says dishes separate. You might think רבי יהושע said this both to be lenient and to be strict. The משנה teaches that he did not say it to be lenient, only to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש explains why the line is needed. The two halves came from two different dishes, and the משנה teaches that they still combine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע holds that two full כזיתים from two dishes give two חטאות. We might think that same separation would stop two halves from combining. In this version, the משנה says no: the separation only works to make things stricter, so the halves still combine and he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Dishes (separate serving bowls)
Dishes separate: each dish counts as its own act for חטאות
What case are we dealing with here?
To be lenient / to be strict

steps.whyThisMatters: This version is what creates the problem. It is a case of separate חטאות where the halves still combine.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר תּוּטֵנִי:
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said in the name of bar Tutni:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where he ate it from two dishes,
and it follows Rabbi Yehoshua,
who said dishes separate.
You might have said that Rabbi Yehoshua said it
both as a leniency and as a stringency;

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דִּלְקוּלָּא לָא אָמַר,
phrases.english: it teaches us that he did not say it as a leniency,
he said it as a stringency.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר תּוּטֵנִי: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is two dishes according to רבי יהושע. Dishes separate only to make things stricter, so the halves still combine.

steps.title: The contradiction: separate for חטאות, yet the halves combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge: in ריש לקיש's case the dishes would give separate חטאות, and still the halves combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here they are separate for חטאות, and still they combine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the contradiction it was building toward since Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהושע, two dishes give two separate חטאות, so this is a case of חלוקין לחטאות. Yet ריש לקיש's version says the halves combine. That goes against Step 12's rule that half-measures needing separate חטאות do not combine.

keyTerms.meaning: But here! (pointing to a contradicting case)

phrases.english: But here, where they are separate for sin-offerings,
and they do combine!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דַּחֲלוּקִין לַחֲטָאוֹת, וְקָא מִצְטָרְפִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses ריש לקיש's explanation (Step 15) to complete the challenge opened in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 12's rule that separate חטאות means no combining
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two dishes give separate חטאות for רבי יהושע, yet in this version the half-measures combine.

steps.title: The answer: it depends which part of the משנה ריש לקיש was explaining
steps.stepSummary: The reply is that the questioner placed ריש לקיש's comment on the רישא. We place it on the סיפא, and then there is no problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You teach ריש לקיש's comment on the first clause, so you have a difficulty. We teach it on the last clause, so we have no difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that there were two versions of where ריש לקיש's comment belongs. The text says only "he said to him"; this is most likely רבי זירא speaking to רבי ירמיה. In the speaker's version, the challenge disappears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difficulty only came from attaching ריש לקיש's comment to the line 'one type, liable.' If it belongs on 'two types, exempt,' ריש לקיש teaches the opposite about רבי יהושע. The next step lays that version out.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה
The last part of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is changing the משנה itself. The only question is which line of the משנה ריש לקיש's comment explains, and that changes what רבי יהושע's rule teaches.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָר אַרֵישָׁא מַתְנֵי לַהּ
phrases.english: He said to him: The Master teaches it on the first clause
and so it is difficult for him.
We teach it on the latter clause,
and it is not difficult for us:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מָר אַרֵישָׁא מַתְנֵי לַהּ וְקַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16 by offering a different version of ריש לקיש's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version (גירסא) of where the statement is placed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש explained the רישא, so two dishes combine despite separate חטאות.
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש explained the סיפא, so two dishes do not combine, which fits Step 12's rule.

steps.title: The סיפא version: 'two types' means two dishes, and רבי יהושע is lenient too
steps.stepSummary: In this version, ריש לקיש says 'two types, exempt' really means one type in two dishes. This shows רבי יהושע's rule works for leniency as well, so the halves do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'From two types he is exempt.' Did that need to be said? ריש לקיש said in the name of בר תוטני: really it is one type. Why does it call it 'two types'? Because he ate it from two dishes, and it follows רבי יהושע, who says dishes separate. This teaches us that רבי יהושע said it both to be lenient and to be strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the version where ריש לקיש's comment explains the סיפא. In it, two dishes keep the halves apart, so the person is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two halves of two truly different types obviously don't combine, so the line must mean something new. It means one type in two dishes. Since 'dishes separate' now works even to be lenient, things that are separate for חטאות do not combine, and Step 12's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (introducing the true meaning)
And why does it call it this?
And this is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of ריש לקיש. On the רישא, רבי יהושע's 'dishes separate' is only strict, and that challenges the rule. On the סיפא, it is both lenient and strict, so things separate for חטאות do not combine, and the rule from Step 12 holds.

phrases.english: "From two types he is exempt": was it necessary to say?

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם בַּר תּוּטֵנִי
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said in the name of bar Tutni:
Actually it is from one type.
And why does it call it "two types"?
Because he ate it from two dishes,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא דְּאָמַר תַּמְחוּיִין מְחַלְּקִין.
phrases.english: and it follows Rabbi Yehoshua, who said dishes separate.
And this is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֵּין לְקוּלָּא בֵּין לְחוּמְרָא.
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua said it both as a leniency and as a stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the סיפא version announced in Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the משנה's wording ('two types' means two dishes)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע's separation by dishes only makes things stricter.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dishes separate even to be lenient, so halves from two dishes do not combine.

steps.title: Starting a new inference from the סיפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to draw a conclusion from the fact that the סיפא is about one type in two dishes. The sentence continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the last clause is about one type in two dishes...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts a new argument from how the סיפא was just explained, and the actual point comes on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'two types' in the סיפא means one type in two dishes, that reading may have consequences for how we understand the רישא. The גמרא is about to use this to make an inference or raise a new question.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that the latter clause...

phrases.english: From the fact that the latter clause is one type
and two dishes,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new argument on the סיפא reading set up in Step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The סיפא version of ריש לקיש's explanation (completed on the next עמוד)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An inference from the סיפא's meaning will be applied to the rest of the משנה.
